body_long:
Louis Vuitton has chosen a fashion executive to run its most ambitious Paris address. Delphine Bellini, the former chief executive of Schiaparelli, is now managing director of the house's future destination at 103 avenue des Champs-Élysées. According to an internal note reported by WWD, she started on 9 November 2026. La Tribune de l'Hôtellerie covered the appointment on 21 November.

## A destination, not a store

Louis Vuitton presents 103 Champs-Élysées as a "retailtainment" destination. The programme combines retail, dining, a café, exhibition spaces and jewellery showcases. The building has been under renovation for about three years, with the architecture firm Barthélémy Griño. Louis Vuitton has not confirmed an opening date.

Hugues Bonnet-Masimbert, commercial director of Louis Vuitton, said he was convinced her vision would deliver the house's highest ambitions in Paris.

## The hotel question

The address was long expected to include a hotel. The original building permit included lodging, and in 2023 the Paris commercial planning commission approved a hotel of about 6,000 m². In January 2026, Bernard Arnault ended that plan, saying Vuitton would not do a hotel. Press reports from early November mention a possible 2027 opening, a two-level restaurant and a handful of ultra-VIP rooms. Louis Vuitton has confirmed none of these details.

## A couture career

Bellini began in luxury tourism, in sales and marketing for cruise companies, including Royal Olympic Cruises. She joined Léonard in 2002 to manage licences, then Jean-Charles de Castelbajac in 2005, where she became deputy managing director. After a period as a transition consultant for fashion and luxury brands, she became chief executive of Schiaparelli in 2014 and led the relaunch of the couture house for about twelve years. She has taught at the Institut Français de la Mode since 2010 and was named by WWD among its 50 powerful women in 2022. Schiaparelli has not yet named her successor.

## The signal

Fashion houses are building places to eat, linger and be seen, on the same avenues as the palaces. When Louis Vuitton hands such a project to a couture leader rather than a hotelier, it shows where the competition for the luxury guest's evening is heading.

Congratulations to Delphine Bellini on her new role.
summary: The former Schiaparelli CEO became managing director of Louis Vuitton's future destination at 103 avenue des Champs-Élysées on 9 November.
title: Delphine Bellini, from Schiaparelli to Louis Vuitton's 103 Champs-Élysées
why: LVMH hands its most ambitious Paris address, once planned with a hotel, to a couture leader.
